# Synapsor Runner

Synapsor Runner is the Apache-2.0 database-authority layer for AI agents. It
lets agents query and propose changes to Postgres/MySQL without giving the
model SQL, credentials, trusted tenant/principal identity, activation,
approval, or commit authority.

Current adoption loop:
Connect staging -> deterministic whole-schema draft -> human boundary review ->
bounded Explore in the CLI, preview Workbench, or an MCP client -> optional
Protect This Query -> digest-bound human activation -> named capability ->
exact proposal -> outside-model decision -> guarded commit -> receipt and replay.

Important boundaries:
- No raw SQL or SQL-string tool argument.
- The operator-only Plan Playground validates or replays the existing fixed
  Explore JSON grammar. It adds no MCP tool and cannot accept trusted scope.
- Scoped Explore is disabled by default. Local development/staging may expose
  exactly `app.describe_data` and `app.explore_data` over stdio or loopback.
  Separately reviewed production Explore may expose those same two read-only
  tools over secured Streamable HTTP only with verified asymmetric JWT claims,
  reviewed budgets, rate limits, and atomic shared-Postgres accounting.
- Aggregate Explore is a reviewed analytical cube: approved measures,
  dimensions, time buckets, filters, and at most three activated paths. Paths
  default to two catalog-proven many-to-one links and may be reviewed up to the
  hard maximum of three, with suppression and extraction/differencing budgets.
- Optional local Workbench Ask can use OpenAI, Anthropic, or a tested
  OpenAI-compatible endpoint, but it calls only the exact reviewed tools and
  adds no activation, approval, or commit authority.
- Auto Boundary and Protect are deterministic and use no LLM.
- Generated authority starts disabled. The model cannot activate, approve,
  apply, commit, or widen it.
- Existing hand-authored 1.x contracts and established CLI routes do not
  require Auto Boundary, Workbench, rescanning, or generation locks.
- Runner-managed direct writes recheck current authority and conflict guards;
  source-database receipt mode can commit the mutation and receipt atomically.
  Runner-ledger mode does not claim distributed exactly-once behavior.
- Rich multi-table transactions and external side effects remain app-owned
  executor work after approval. The application owns final scope, conflict,
  idempotency, transaction, rollback, and receipt behavior.
